newsitem.title: GERMANY: Koebnick-doesn't see EMU delay but may be mulled.
newsitem.headline: Koebnick-doesn't see EMU delay but may be mulled.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said on Monday that he did not at present think European monetary union would be postponed but added that he thought a delay would be considered.
"For the time being I don't think they will change the calendar but I think they will think it over," Koebnick told reporters at a reception.

Koebnick also said that in order to reach a compromise in the Bundesbank's dispute with the Bonn government over gold revaluation, the government would need to drop its demand for a payout in 1997 from the reserve revaluation.
Koebnick said it was problematic "that the government doesn't see room to manoeuvre" on meeting the EMU critera without resorting to the revaluation.
He also said that he doubted EMU could start or be successful unless Germany and France take part.
